hook.line: Meeting minutes, statutes and contracts keep opening sentences with a single word like *aprobado* or *firmado*. Learn to spot it and the whole formal register gets easier to read, and to write.
hook.es: Dicho esto, pasemos al siguiente punto.
hook.en: Having said that, let's move on to the next point.

examples.es: Una vez aprobado el plan, comenzarán las obras.
examples.en: Once the plan is approved, work will begin.

examples.es: Terminada la reunión, todos se fueron.
examples.en: Once the meeting was over, everyone left.

examples.es: Firmados los estatutos, la cooperativa existe.
examples.en: Once the statutes are signed, the cooperative exists.

examples.es: Hecho el pago, recibirá el recibo.
examples.en: Once the payment is made, you will receive the receipt. (formal)

examples.es: Cerrada la votación, se contaron los votos.
examples.en: Once the vote was closed, the votes were counted.

examples.es: Resuelto el problema, abrimos otra vez.
examples.en: Once the problem was solved, we opened again.

rule:
Each example opens with a past participle followed by the thing it describes: *aprobado el plan*, *terminada la reunión*. No *haber*, no *que*, no extra verb. It is a shortcut for "once that was done".

The participle agrees with its noun like an adjective:
*aprobado el plan*
*aprobada la propuesta*
*firmados los estatutos*

The phrase only sets the scene, so the main clause can be about something else: *Terminada la reunión, todos se fueron.* It almost always comes first.

Add *una vez* in front to make the timing obvious: *Una vez aprobado el plan*. English has a faint cousin in "that done"; Spanish uses it everywhere in writing. *Dicho esto* ("that said") is a set phrase for moving on.
smallPrint: Teachers call these absolute constructions: the participle clause has its own subject, separate from the main clause. They are much more common in writing than in speech.

readAndPick.es: Una vez aprobado el plan, comenzarán las obras.
options: Work will begin before the plan is approved.
Once the plan is approved, work will begin.

readAndPick.es: Terminada la reunión, todos se fueron.
options: Once the meeting was over, everyone left.
Everyone left before the meeting ended.

readAndPick.es: Firmados los estatutos, la cooperativa existe.
options: Once the statute is signed, the cooperative exists.
Once the statutes are signed, the cooperative exists.

readAndPick.es: Una vez firmado el estatuto, la cooperativa existe.
options: Once the statute is signed, the cooperative exists.
Once the statutes are signed, the cooperative exists.

readAndPick.es: Cerrada la votación, se contaron los votos.
options: Once the votes were counted, the vote was closed.
Once the vote was closed, the votes were counted.

readAndPick.es: Hecho el pago, recibirá el recibo.
options: Once the payment is made, you will receive the receipt. (formal)
Once the receipt arrives, you will make the payment. (formal)

readAndPick.es: Resuelto el problema, abrimos otra vez.
options: Once we opened again, the problem was solved.
Once the problem was solved, we opened again.

readAndPick.es: Dicho esto, pasemos al siguiente punto.
options: That said, let's move on to the next point.
That said, they moved on to the next point.

readAndPick.es: Una vez recibidos los aportes, se repartirán las ganancias.
options: Once the profits are split, the contributions will be received.
Once the contributions are received, the profits will be split.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *aprobado* or *aprobada* and type the whole sentence: Una vez ___ la propuesta, comenzarán las obras.
yourTurn.answer: Una vez aprobada la propuesta, comenzarán las obras.
yourTurn.why: The participle agrees with *propuesta*, which is feminine.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *firmado* or *firmados* and type the whole sentence: ___ los estatutos, la cooperativa existe.
yourTurn.answer: Firmados los estatutos, la cooperativa existe.
accept: Una vez firmados los estatutos, la cooperativa existe.
yourTurn.why: *Estatutos* is plural, so the participle is plural too.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Once the meeting was over, everyone left.
yourTurn.answer: Terminada la reunión, todos se fueron.
accept: Una vez terminada la reunión, todos se fueron.
yourTurn.why: Participle first, matching *reunión*, then the main clause.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Having said that, let's move on to the next point.
yourTurn.answer: Dicho esto, pasemos al siguiente punto.
yourTurn.why: *Dicho esto* is a ready-made phrase for changing the subject.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Once the vote was closed, the votes were counted.
yourTurn.answer: Cerrada la votación, se contaron los votos.
accept: Una vez cerrada la votación, se contaron los votos.

yourTurn.prompt: Shorten it with a participle: *Una vez que aprobaron el plan, comenzaron las obras.*
yourTurn.answer: Una vez aprobado el plan, comenzaron las obras.
accept: Aprobado el plan, comenzaron las obras.
yourTurn.why: Drop *que* and the verb, keep the participle and the noun.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *Una vez firmado el contrato, Tomás abrió el café.* (Two contracts.)
yourTurn.answer: Una vez firmados los contratos, Tomás abrió el café.
yourTurn.why: Both the article and the participle follow the noun into the plural.

pitfalls.wrong: Una vez terminar la reunión, todos se fueron.
pitfalls.right: Una vez terminada la reunión, todos se fueron.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *una vez* Spanish wants the participle, which agrees with *reunión*.

pitfalls.wrong: Una vez aprobado la propuesta, comenzarán las obras.
pitfalls.right: Una vez aprobada la propuesta, comenzarán las obras.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The participle is an adjective here, so it matches *propuesta*.

pitfalls.wrong: Una vez que aprobado el plan, comenzarán las obras.
pitfalls.right: Una vez aprobado el plan, comenzarán las obras.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Una vez que* needs a full verb; with a participle, leave *que* out.

personal: Think of something you did this week in a fixed order. Say it in two steps, starting with *Una vez* and a participle, for example *Una vez terminado el trabajo*, and then what you did next.
